questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

If no substitution is required, select No improvement.

__I am think that tomorrow I will take__ leave and stay at home.

options.text: I have thought tomorrow I am taking
I think that tomorrow I will take
I was thinking that the next day I will be taking

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

The verb form **think** does not go in agreement with **am.** Therefore the correction would be to omit **Am** which is used with the present continuous form of the verb i.e. thinking. So, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

They opened a new mall nearby last month.

options.text: Nearby a new mall is opened last month with them.
A new mall can be open be nearby last month by him.
A new mall was opened nearby last month by them.
A new mall will be opened nearby last month by him.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

The given sentence has **they **as the** subject **and** mall **as the** object.** So a change in voice will make **mall **as the** subject.** Also, the action was performed in the past. So, we will use the past tense of the verb i.e **was opened.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

The word **by whom** changes to **who **in the active voice. Also, the sentence is clearly in the past tense as the word **taught** is used. So, option 2 is correct.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Selected the option that gives their correct order.

A. When we can't laugh at the same joke again, why should we cry over the same problems?

B. One day he told them a joke and everyone roared with laughter.

C. People came to a wise man to complain about the same problems every time.

D. When he repeated the joke twice, nobody laughed anymore.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

The first sentence should be **C** as it tells us what is being talked about and gives a suitable beginning.

Next, should be **B** as it describes the incident of one day.

After B it should be **D **as A gives the conclusion as to what the man was trying to convey through his act.

So,** A** should be at the end.

**The correct sequence is : CBDA.**

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Having just taking a heavy lunch, she was not ready to have any fruit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**taking a heavy lunch'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In this part of the sentence, there is an error in the given part - '**taking a heavy lunch'**.
 
• '**taking**' should be replaced by '**taken**'.
 
• The structure '**having taken**' is a **perfect participle **which functions as an **adverbial modifier of time**.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence is- '**Having just taken __a heavy lunch, she was not ready to have any fruit.'**

Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

 
• An** adverbial modifier **is a word or phrase that modifies another part of a sentence, typically a verb or adjective.

 
 
• **Adverbs of time** tell us when an action happened, but also for **how long, and how often.** Adverbs of time are **invariable**. 
 
• Soon now, later, then, tomorrow, today, day after tomorrow, everyday, weekly, annually, quarterly, yearly, yesterday, last month, tonight, last week, immediately, etc. are some examples of **adverbs of time.**
